content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] staged-release watcher detected sustained 503 spike on service: inference-api-canary (us-east-1). rolling window: 5m, error rate: 12% (> threshold 5%). auto-pager triggered.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: INC-2026-3145 opened and routed to on-call: jun. Escalation policy: deploy-critical -> 10m. Link: <https://pd.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-3145|INC-2026-3145>.

jun: acked. I'm on it. quick question — is this across all canaries or only this release wave?

kyle: saw the alert in telemetry. looks canary-only so far (us-east-1 single ASG). spike started ~2m after traffic ramp to 5%. logs show a flurry of 503s from router -> backend timeout.

sara: adding customer-impact note: internal metric shows ~3% global user-facing requests affected (likely routed through that region). some customers are seeing request timeouts in sessions. notifying support.

jun: thanks. can someone grab the canary pods logs and tracer spans? paste useful snippets here. I want to check downstream auth/service timeouts.

product-sre: grabbing logs now, tailing:
```
[2026-03-12T15:03:02Z] inference-api-canary-7f4b: upstream timeout after 10s -> 503
[2026-03-12T15:03:05Z] inference-api-canary-7f4b: kv-cache-miss spike concurrent 60 -> added latency
```

ops-lead: what was the exact rollout command used? did we push a sidecar or a model change in this wave?

kyle: deployment hash: sha256:af3c9..; release tag: release/2026-03-12-canary-quant; only config change was a small kernel-opt flag and bumped model artifact to v1.2-quant. no sidecar changes.

jun: ok probable regression surface: quantized model path + kernel flag under load. mitigation plan: 1) pause further rollouts, 2) divert traffic off canary (scale down canary weight), 3) consider rollback of canary to previous model.

ops-lead: agreed. pausing rollout now. Jun, can you scale canary weight to 0 with the traffic manager? I'm ready to flip if you advise.

jun: doing now. command: 
```
./trafficctl set-weight inference-api canary us-east-1 0 --reason "503 spike"
```

incident-bot: action recorded: traffic weight updated for inference-api canary us-east-1 -> 0 by jun.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-3145 status: acknowledged by jun. next escalation in 10m.

sara: support notified customers in affected cohort and opened incident customer thread. PR for status page update in progress.

jun: next steps: collect full pod logs and CPU/GPU telemetry for that canary slice, run a rollback test on staging to validate behavior, then either rollback canary to release/2026-03-10-stable or keep diversion until canary patch ready. tagging ops-lead for rollback approval.

ops-lead: approve rollback to stable if metrics don't normalize in 8 minutes. I'll coordinate with infra for a quick rollback.

product-sre: capturing data snapshot, including p50/p95 latency pre/post ramp, kv-cache hit ratio, and kernel metric counters. uploading to incident folder: <https://drive.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-3145/data|incident data>.

jun: thumbs up. updating PD note: "Traffic diverted from canary, investigating model quantization path and kernel flag under load. customer impact limited; rolling rollback if not recovered."

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-3145: note added by jun.

ops-lead: if rollback approved, command to rollback will be: 
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-api --to-revision=2026-03-10-stable --namespace=prod-us-east-1
```

jun: leaving a temp watch on this thread, will update within 5m with telemetry after diversion. anyone else who wants to join the bridge ping me.

kyle: joining for logs. ping me if you want me to run a quick A/B canary test on staging.

incident-bot: reminder: autopage will escalate to ops-lead in 7m if still unacked/unsolved.

(last update) jun: diversion complete, error rate dropped from 12% -> 1.1% in 90s after weight=0. keeping PD open while we validate longer tail and decide rollback vs patch.
